extraction.name: LAMBADA
extraction.description: LAMBADA is a collection of narrative passages sharing the characteristic that human subjects are able to guess their last word if they are exposed to the whole passage, but not if they only see the last sentence preceding the target word.
extraction.creator: Denis Papemo, Germán Kruszewski, Angeliki Lazaridou, Quan Ngoc Pham, Raffaella Bemardi, Sandro Pezzelle, Marco Baroni, Gemma Boleda, Raquel Femández
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Passages were extracted from the Book Corpus, filtered using language models to remove easy cases, and then evaluated by human subjects via crowdsourcing to ensure the target word could only be guessed with the broad context.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The Book Corpus, which contains unpublished novels.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Duplicate removal, filtering out potentially offensive material with a stop word list, and filtering out passages whose target word had probability >= 0.00175 according to any of four language models.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: One human subject guessed the target word based on the whole passage; if right, a second subject guessed based on the whole passage; if also right, up to 10 subjects tried to guess based on the target sentence only. If no subject guessed it from the sentence alone, it was added.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A strict hit-or-miss approach was used, requiring two consecutive subjects to exactly match the missing word from the broad context, and ensuring no subject out of ten could provide it based on local context only.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Up to 12 human labels per item (2 for the whole passage, and up to 10 for the target sentence only).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Four language models: a pre-trained recurrent neural network (RNN) and three models trained on the Book Corpus (a standard 4-gram model, a RNN and a feed-forward model).
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Proper nouns are hugely over-represented in LAMBADA (48%), while other categories like verbs, adjectives, and adverbs are under-represented compared to the POS distribution in the input.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Standard language models are bound to fail on it by design because passages where simple language models succeeded were filtered out during data collection.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluating computational models for text understanding (word prediction). Development data can be used for fine-tuning.

name.evidence: We introduce LAMBADA, a dataset to evaluate the capabilities of computational models for text understanding by means of a word prediction task.

description.evidence: LAMBADA is a collection of narrative passages sharing the characteristic that human subjects are able to guess their last word if they are exposed to the whole passage, but not if they only see the last sentence preceding the target word.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: In fact, proper nouns are hugely over-represented in LAMBADA, while the other categories are under-represented, compared to the POS distribution in the input.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: We also note that, because of the way we have constructed LAMBADA, standard language models are bound to fail on it by design: one of our first filters (see Section 3.1) was to choose passages where a number of simple language models were failing to predict the upcoming word.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We thus propose LAMBADA as a challenging test set, meant to encourage the development of new models capable of genuine understanding of broad context in natural language text... The development data can be used to fine-tune models to the specifics of the LAMBADA passages.
